title: Chemistry: Polyatomic Ions and Common Compounds

sources.name: Original educational synthesis from general knowledge

description: For chemistry students learning common polyatomic ions, ionic formulas and naming rules. Plain-text formulas use digits for atom counts and caret notation for ionic charges.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of ammonium?
cards.example: NH4Cl contains one ammonium ion per chloride ion.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of hydroxide?
cards.example: NaOH contains one hydroxide ion per sodium ion.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of nitrate?
cards.example: Ca(NO3)2 contains two nitrate ions per calcium ion.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of nitrite?
cards.example: NaNO2 is sodium nitrite.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of sulfate?
cards.example: Na2SO4 balances one sulfate ion with two sodium ions.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of sulfite?
cards.example: Na2SO3 is sodium sulfite.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of hydrogen sulfate?
cards.example: NaHSO4 contains hydrogen sulfate.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of hydrogen sulfite?
cards.example: NaHSO3 contains hydrogen sulfite.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of carbonate?
cards.example: CaCO3 pairs calcium with carbonate.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of hydrogen carbonate?
cards.example: NaHCO3 is sodium hydrogen carbonate.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of phosphate?
cards.example: Na3PO4 balances phosphate with three sodium ions.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of hydrogen phosphate?
cards.example: Na2HPO4 contains hydrogen phosphate.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of dihydrogen phosphate?
cards.example: NaH2PO4 contains dihydrogen phosphate.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of acetate?
cards.back: CH3COO^-; charge -1. C2H3O2^- is another common notation.
cards.example: CH3COONa is sodium acetate.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of cyanide?
cards.example: NaCN is sodium cyanide.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of thiocyanate?
cards.example: KSCN is potassium thiocyanate.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of permanganate?
cards.example: KMnO4 is potassium permanganate.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of chromate?
cards.example: K2CrO4 is potassium chromate.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of dichromate?
cards.example: K2Cr2O7 is potassium dichromate.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of hypochlorite?
cards.example: NaClO is sodium hypochlorite.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of chlorite?
cards.example: NaClO2 is sodium chlorite.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of chlorate?
cards.example: KClO3 is potassium chlorate.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of perchlorate?
cards.example: KClO4 is potassium perchlorate.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of bromate?
cards.example: KBrO3 is potassium bromate.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of iodate?
cards.example: KIO3 is potassium iodate.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of oxalate?
cards.example: Na2C2O4 is sodium oxalate.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of peroxide?
cards.example: Na2O2 contains the peroxide ion.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of hydronium?
cards.example: H3O^+ represents protonated water in acid-base equations.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of thiosulfate?
cards.example: Na2S2O3 is sodium thiosulfate.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of hydrogen oxalate?
cards.example: NaHC2O4 contains hydrogen oxalate.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of formate?
cards.example: HCOONa is sodium formate.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of azide?
cards.example: NaN3 is sodium azide.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of superoxide?
cards.example: KO2 contains superoxide.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of cyanate?
cards.example: KOCN is potassium cyanate.

cards.front: What are the formula and charge of manganate?
cards.example: K2MnO4 contains manganate, not permanganate.

cards.front: What is the formula of sodium nitrate?
cards.example: Formula-writing practice: sodium nitrate is represented by NaNO3.

cards.front: What is the formula of potassium nitrate?
cards.example: Formula-writing practice: potassium nitrate is represented by KNO3.

cards.example: Formula-writing practice: calcium nitrate is represented by Ca(NO3)2.

cards.front: What is the formula of ammonium nitrate?
cards.example: Formula-writing practice: ammonium nitrate is represented by NH4NO3.

cards.front: What is the formula of sodium nitrite?
cards.example: Formula-writing practice: sodium nitrite is represented by NaNO2.

cards.front: What is the formula of sodium sulfate?
cards.example: Formula-writing practice: sodium sulfate is represented by Na2SO4.

cards.front: What is the formula of magnesium sulfate?
cards.example: Formula-writing practice: magnesium sulfate is represented by MgSO4, for the anhydrous compound.

cards.front: What is the formula of aluminum sulfate?
cards.example: Formula-writing practice: aluminum sulfate is represented by Al2(SO4)3.

cards.front: What is the formula of ammonium sulfate?

cards.example: Formula-writing practice: copper(II) sulfate is represented by CuSO4, for the anhydrous compound.

cards.front: What is the formula of iron(III) sulfate?
cards.example: Formula-writing practice: iron(III) sulfate is represented by Fe2(SO4)3.

cards.front: What is the formula of sodium sulfite?
cards.example: Formula-writing practice: sodium sulfite is represented by Na2SO3.

cards.front: What is the formula of sodium hydrogen sulfate?
cards.example: Formula-writing practice: sodium hydrogen sulfate is represented by NaHSO4.

cards.front: What is the formula of sodium carbonate?
cards.example: Formula-writing practice: sodium carbonate is represented by Na2CO3.

cards.front: What is the formula of sodium hydrogen carbonate?
cards.example: Formula-writing practice: sodium hydrogen carbonate is represented by NaHCO3.

cards.front: What is the formula of calcium carbonate?
cards.example: Formula-writing practice: calcium carbonate is represented by CaCO3.

cards.front: What is the formula of ammonium carbonate?
cards.example: Formula-writing practice: ammonium carbonate is represented by (NH4)2CO3.

cards.front: What is the formula of sodium phosphate?
cards.example: Formula-writing practice: sodium phosphate is represented by Na3PO4, also called trisodium phosphate.

cards.example: Formula-writing practice: calcium phosphate, using orthophosphate ions is represented by Ca3(PO4)2.

cards.example: Formula-writing practice: disodium hydrogen phosphate is represented by Na2HPO4.

cards.example: Formula-writing practice: sodium dihydrogen phosphate is represented by NaH2PO4.

cards.example: Formula-writing practice: sodium hydroxide is represented by NaOH.

cards.example: Formula-writing practice: calcium hydroxide is represented by Ca(OH)2.

cards.example: Formula-writing practice: magnesium hydroxide is represented by Mg(OH)2.

cards.front: What is the formula of aluminum hydroxide?
cards.example: Formula-writing practice: aluminum hydroxide is represented by Al(OH)3.

cards.front: What is the formula of iron(III) hydroxide?
cards.example: Formula-writing practice: iron(III) hydroxide is represented by Fe(OH)3.

cards.front: What is the formula of sodium acetate?
cards.example: Formula-writing practice: sodium acetate is represented by CH3COONa; also written NaC2H3O2.

cards.front: What is the formula of calcium acetate?
cards.example: Formula-writing practice: calcium acetate is represented by Ca(CH3COO)2.

cards.front: What is the formula of potassium permanganate?
cards.example: Formula-writing practice: potassium permanganate is represented by KMnO4.

cards.front: What is the formula of potassium dichromate?
cards.example: Formula-writing practice: potassium dichromate is represented by K2Cr2O7.

cards.front: What is the formula of sodium hypochlorite?
cards.back: NaClO; NaOCl is an equivalent ordering.
cards.example: Formula-writing practice: sodium hypochlorite is represented by NaClO; NaOCl is an equivalent ordering.

cards.front: What is the formula of potassium chlorate?
cards.example: Formula-writing practice: potassium chlorate is represented by KClO3.

cards.front: What is the formula of ammonium chloride?
cards.example: Formula-writing practice: ammonium chloride is represented by NH4Cl.

cards.front: What is the formula of sodium peroxide?
cards.example: Formula-writing practice: sodium peroxide is represented by Na2O2.

cards.front: What is the formula of hydrogen peroxide?
cards.back: H2O2. It is a neutral molecular compound.
cards.example: Formula-writing practice: hydrogen peroxide is represented by H2O2.

cards.front: What is the formula of sodium thiosulfate?
cards.example: Formula-writing practice: sodium thiosulfate is represented by Na2S2O3, for the anhydrous compound.

cards.front: What does a subscript outside parentheses multiply in Ca(NO3)2?
cards.back: Every atom inside the parentheses: two nitrogen atoms and six oxygen atoms.
cards.example: Apply this rule when reading formulas such as Ca(NO3)2 and Na2SO4.

cards.front: Why does Ca(NO3)2 contain two nitrate ions?
cards.back: One Ca^2+ requires two NO3^- ions to make the formula unit electrically neutral.
cards.example: Apply this rule when reading formulas such as Ca(NO3)2 and Na2SO4.

cards.front: What total charge must a neutral ionic compound's formula have?
cards.back: Zero; positive and negative ionic charges balance.
cards.example: Apply this rule when reading formulas such as Ca(NO3)2 and Na2SO4.

cards.front: How do nitrate and nitrite differ in oxygen count?
cards.back: Nitrate has three oxygen atoms; nitrite has two. Both have charge -1.
cards.example: Apply this rule when reading formulas such as Ca(NO3)2 and Na2SO4.

cards.front: How do sulfate and sulfite differ in oxygen count?
cards.back: Sulfate has four oxygen atoms; sulfite has three. Both have charge -2.
cards.example: Apply this rule when reading formulas such as Ca(NO3)2 and Na2SO4.

cards.front: Within the chlorine oxyanion series, what does per-...-ate indicate?
cards.back: Perchlorate has one more oxygen than chlorate: ClO4^- versus ClO3^-.
cards.example: Apply this rule when reading formulas such as Ca(NO3)2 and Na2SO4.

cards.front: Within the chlorine oxyanion series, what does hypo-...-ite indicate?
cards.back: Hypochlorite has one fewer oxygen than chlorite: ClO^- versus ClO2^-.
cards.example: Apply this rule when reading formulas such as Ca(NO3)2 and Na2SO4.

cards.front: What does the Roman numeral in iron(III) sulfate specify?
cards.back: The oxidation state of iron: +3. It does not give the number of iron atoms.
cards.example: Apply this rule when reading formulas such as Ca(NO3)2 and Na2SO4.

cards.front: What does the dot in CuSO4·5H2O represent?
cards.back: Five water molecules per formula unit in the hydrate, copper(II) sulfate pentahydrate.
cards.example: Apply this rule when reading formulas such as Ca(NO3)2 and Na2SO4.
